title: SIG Questionnaire Walkthrough - Harmony Finance
summary: Walkthrough of customer's SIG/CAIQ-style vendor risk questionnaire. Covered SOC 2, ISO, SSO/RBAC, audit logs, encryption and KMS, data residency, and evidence requests. SE answered architecture and deployment questions (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Agreed next steps: share SOC 2 report, security pack, KMS diagram, and schedule infra deep-dive. Customer to confirm required evidence and timeline.
topics: Encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration
Data residency and VPC/private deployment options
action_items: Owner: Maya Patel; Item: Send Redwood security pack + SOC 2 Type II report; Due: 2025-12-04
Owner: Jordan Lee; Item: Provide KMS integration diagram (customer-managed KMS flow) and notes on envelope encryption; Due: 2025-12-05
Owner: Priya Sharma (Harmony); Item: Confirm list of mandatory evidence for procurement (SIG vs CAIQ vs custom form) and deadlines; Due: 2025-12-09
Owner: Marcus Chen (Harmony); Item: Schedule infra deep-dive with engineering (45m) to validate networking/VPC requirements; Due: 2025-12-07
next_steps: Redwood to upload SOC2 report and security pack to shared folder
SE to prepare KMS/encryption diagram and sample audit log extract
Customer to mark required evidence fields in the SIG spreadsheet and return
Schedule technical deep-dive (networking and private deployment options) next week
transcript:
Header: Date: 2025-12-02 | Start: 15:00 PST | Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Evan Brooks (Redwood), Lena Ortiz (Harmony - Head of Security), Marcus Chen (Harmony - VP Eng), Priya Sharma (Harmony - Compliance), Samir Rao (Harmony - Procurement)

Summary (auto): quick walkthrough of the SIG/CAIQ vendor questionnaire, clarifying evidence types and deployment models.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone thanks for making time, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'll do a quick intro and then Jordan will run through the SIG questions.
00:18 Lena: Thanks Maya, appreciate it. We just want to make sure we can close the vendor risk process by end of month, so we'll go through the questionnaire and flag anything that needs evidence.
00:28 Jordan: Awesome, yeah I'll share my screen in a sec. So at high level we'll follow the SIG spreadsheet, starting with Org security and then infra, encryption, access control, etc. Feel free to stop and ask.
00:45 Marcus: Quick ask up front — we run in multiple regions and have strict data residency for EU customers, so please call out where data might persist.
00:56 Jordan: Yup noted, we'll cover Redwood hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and how data residency works in each.
01:20 Priya: For procurement we typically need SOC 2 Type II and a recent penetration test report, also SSO details.
01:33 Maya: We have SOC 2 Type II, and we'll share the latest report. For pen test we can share summary and remediation notes.
01:46 Jordan: Jumping into the questionnaire — Control: Access Control / RBAC. Question: Do you provide role-based access controls and can roles be customized? Answer: yes, Redwood Console supports RBAC with pre-set roles and custom roles at the org and project level.
02:10 Lena: And SAML? We use Okta.
02:14 Jordan: SSO via SAML 2.0 and OIDC supported, SAML metadata exchange is standard. We have guidance in the docs for Okta/OneLogin.
02:30 Lena: Any gotchas around just-in-time provisioning?
02:34 Jordan: Currently we support SCIM for user provisioning in the Private and Dedicated offers, hosted will be scoping soon — actually small correction, hosted supports SAML SSO for auth but provisioning via SCIM is available on Dedicated and Private.
02:52 Samir: Ok that matters for our identity sync requirement.
03:05 Jordan: Next: Audit logging — we store audit logs for actions within the Console, and customers can export logs to their SIEM. Retention default is 90 days for hosted; Dedicated/Private can be configured to meet customer retention requirements.
03:22 Marcus: Can we get raw audit logs for e-discovery? Format?
03:26 Jordan: Yeah we can provide JSONL exports with timestamps, actor, action, resource path. We'll attach a sample extract. There's sometimes slight differences in field names in the export, sorry transcription says fileds -> fields.
03:45 Evan: Quick note on redaction — any PII inside logs is hashed/removed by default in hosted, and Dedicated/Private can be configured per policy.
03:58 Lena: Encryption — at rest and in transit? KMS?
04:03 Jordan: All traffic TLS 1.2+ in transit. At rest we use AES-256. For KMS we support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS and GCP KMS for Private and Dedicated. In the hosted case, CMK is supported for enterprise plans — you can bring your own key.
04:28 Priya: How does envelope encryption work? Where are the keys stored?
04:33 Jordan: Envelope encryption: data keys are wrapped by a master key in KMS. The KMS master keys are in the customer's cloud account for Private deployments; for Hosted, keys can either be Redwood-managed or a customer key stored in the cloud provider via cross-account grant. We'll send a diagram.
04:55 Marcus: Is hardware HSM supported?
04:58 Jordan: Yes, via customer-managed HSM linked to KMS providers — we can provide notes for HSM integration.
05:10 Lena: Data residency — where could a customer prompt or data be stored? We are concerned about EU-only residency for certain workloads.
05:18 Jordan: By default hosted routes data to region-based clusters; we can pin workloads to specific regions for EU. Dedicated is in customer's region/pool and Private is fully customer controlled in VPC. We'll need to confirm your retention/processing requirements to advise the right option.
05:42 Priya: For our contract we need assurance that no data crosses borders for EU-labeled customers.
05:48 Maya: For that we recommend Dedicated or Private; hosted can be region-pinned but if you need stricter guarantees Private is the safest. We'll capture that in the follow-up.
06:05 Samir: On the SIG spreadsheet there's a question about third-party sub processors. Can you list major cloud providers and any infra partners?
06:13 Jordan: Sure — AWS, GCP, and select edge partners; we'll provide a subprocessor list and data flow map.
06:26 Lena: Audit/Compliance — ISO 27001?
06:29 Maya: Redwood is ISO 27001 in progress / targeted this quarter — we have controls mapped and can share the roadmap. (slight pause) We do currently have SOC 2 Type II.
06:45 Priya: Pen test — do you provide the full report or an executive summary?
06:49 Evan: Typically we provide an executive summary plus remediation board. Full redacted reports can be shared under NDA in some cases.
07:05 Marcus: Ok good. Next there's a block on network security — VPC peering, IP allowlists, private link?
07:15 Jordan: Dedicated and Private support VPC peering and Private Link options, IP allowlists are supported for management plane endpoints. For hosted, we have an access gateway for private connections on enterprise plans.
07:36 Lena: Latency concerns — any observed effect when we use private link or dedicated routing?
07:41 Jordan: Minimal added hop; we usually see sub-10ms overhead inside region, variable by workload. We can run a benchmark if you'd like during the POC.
07:57 Marcus: That'd be helpful, yes.
08:05 Jordan: Now the SIG question about data lifecycle and deletion: We support data deletion APIs and can purge customer data on request; backups retention windows are disclosed and we can accommodate contractual requirements for deletion timelines.
08:20 Priya: We require proof of deletion for decommissioned tenants. Is there a certificate or audit log?
08:26 Jordan: We can provide deletion audit logs and a signed attestation for big contracts; we'll add that as an evidence item.
08:36 Samir: On legal, our procurement team needs the standard liability limits and SLAs — we'll pull that into the procurement checklist.
08:44 Maya: We can share the standard contract and SLA addendum; legal can talk to your procurement directly if needed.
08:53 Jordan: Back to the SIG — there's an item about application security: secure development lifecycle and code review. We have secure SDLC practices, static analysis, dependency scanning, and regular threat modeling.
09:11 Lena: Who runs threat modeling and frequency?
09:14 Evan: Our security team runs annual threat models for major features and does rolling threat assessments for infra changes. We'll provide policy references.
09:27 Priya: Regarding the CAIQ matrix, some fields ask for control narratives and evidence links. Is there a canonical location you provide for evidence?
09:36 Maya: Yes we typically provide a security pack in a shared secure folder with SOC2 report, pen test summary, subprocessor list, architecture diagrams, and sample audit logs. We'll upload after this call.
09:50 Marcus: Good. A couple specific SIG items: "Key management control" — do you log key usage?
09:57 Jordan: We record KMS API events in audit logs with key id, API action, actor, and timestamp. We'll include a sample KMS audit extract.
10:09 Lena: For hosted, who has access to keys?
10:13 Jordan: For hosted Redwood-managed keys, Redwood platform ops has key access under strict separation of duties and logging. For CMK in customer's account, Redwood never has access to the unwrapped key material. We'll document the exact controls.
10:29 Priya: Encryption in model inference — where does the unencrypted prompt live?
10:33 Jordan: During inference the plaintext exists in memory on the inference node; we use ephemeral memory and ensure KV cache handling respects encryption boundaries. For private deployments that's inside your VPC so your controls apply. There's some slight phrasing variance — we might call it K-V cache.
10:56 Marcus: Any certifications around memory-safe execution?
10:59 Evan: Not a formal cert, but we do memory hardening, process isolation per model instance and periodic fuzz testing. We'll add the test cadence.
11:12 Lena: Ok evidence — we'll need the SOC2 report, pen test summary, KMS diagram, audit log sample, subprocessor list, and an exportable SIG/CAIQ with control IDs filled where you can.
11:25 Maya: That's doable. Jordan, can you check the SIG spreadsheet and pre-fill the easy answers then flag the ones needing more evidence?
11:31 Jordan: Yes I can pre-fill controls where we have canned responses and then mark the ones requiring docs.
11:38 Priya: Timeline — procurement wants to complete vendor risk in 2 weeks. Is that workable?
11:44 Maya: If you return the marked SIG by Friday and we upload the pack early next week, two weeks is tight but plausible. We may need the infra deep-dive done early.
11:55 Marcus: We'll try to get the marked sheet back by Thursday EOD.
12:02 Samir: One more legal thing — data processing addendum and sub-processor notification periods?
12:08 Maya: Standard DPA with 30-day notification for new sub-processors; we can negotiate terms if needed.
12:16 Lena: Great. Anything else?
12:20 Jordan: I'll note a few follow-ups: KMS diagram, audit log sample, SOC2 upload, subprocessor list.
12:29 Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a shared folder link.
12:34 Priya: Thanks, bye.

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription errors and run-ons, proper nouns like K-V cache or K V cache may appear inconsistently.
